Kawasaki Is Bringing a Motorcycle With Legs to EICMA, Plans to Really Make It From 2035
15 photos
Photo: Kawasaki
It's been more than a year since Japanese bike maker Kawasaki came out, during the Osaka Expo 2025, with a vehicle the likes of which the world had never seen before. Part motorcycle, because at its core that's what it is, part dog, because it looks like one, and part horse, because it can carry a human on its back, the so-called Corleo will be making its public debut in Europe next week.
A product of Kawasaki Heavy Industries, the Corleo will be shown by Kawasaki Motors Europe at the Esposizione Internazionale Ciclo Motociclo e Accessori (EICMA) show, which opens its doors in Milan, Italy, at the beginning of November.
In all fairness, show is a bit of a strong word, as the company won't be bringing on the floor of the Fiera Milano Rho an actual, working prototype, but a full-scale mock-up. That's a bit disappointing, true, then again, it's much better than the computer-generated video of the Corleo in action we got last spring.
But what is this thing, after all? Officially a Robotic Multi-legged Vehicle (RMV), the machine is described as a new type of personal mobility vehicle. It was engineered with legs instead of wheels, and it's supposed to take its riders to places that are not easily accessible, not even on the backs of off-road motorcycles. Like, say, climbing mountains.
Kawasaki never revealed what frame the design is imagined around, but it did say its heart is a 150cc hydrogen engine fed by a canister holding the precious substance mounted at the rear.
The electricity the engine generates is used, among other things, to move the design's four legs by pouring into drive units installed inside each of them. The Japanese have not provided any details of the actual capabilities of this system.
Ok, so robots such as this we've seen before, so nothing spectacular there. But the way the Corleo has been imagined to operate is something out of this world, as it involves a human mounting it and riding it as they would a horse.
In a nutshell, the design can be ridden and steered using rider weight-shift inputs sent into a series of steps and handlebars. To make sure the Corleo doesn't slip or trip and hurt its rider, each of its legs is equipped with left-right divided rubber hooves.
Along with the announcement that the Corleo is coming to EICMA 2026 , Kawasaki also shared a few more details about the design, many of which have been kept under wraps until now. For instance, we learned that a special navigation system will be developed for it.
The goal of this system is to factor in all available data on weather, temperature, surface conditions, and even the presence of wildlife, so that riders can be guided on safe routes while in the wild.
This route will be displayed on the instrument panel we already knew the contraption comes with, which also shows hydrogen levels, directions, and rider position. Additionally, the navigation solution will also be available on various undisclosed smart devices.
Back when it was first announced, the Corleo, which also went by the name Concept 01, was just an insane idea, and there were no actual plans to produce it. That has changed in the meantime, and Kawasaki now says it will go for full commercialization by the middle of next decade.

Shipping operators face a new compliance burden under the UK Emissions Trading Scheme (UK ETS) – a £100 ($133) penalty for every missing allowance, adding financial pressure to a regime that will bring offshore vessels into scope from January.
The requirements were outlined in a webinar hosted by Normec, which detailed the monitoring, reporting and allowance-surrender obligations facing vessel operators under the scheme.
Operators of ships above 5,000 gross tonnes must monitor emissions of carbon dioxide, methane, and nitrous oxide, submit verified annual emissions reports, and surrender allowances to cover their liabilities.
A key early hurdle is obtaining regulatory approval for an emissions-monitoring plan. Operators must apply within 42 days of their first maritime activity or port call in the UK, according to the webinar.
Without an approved plan, operators risk complications with the verification process, with site visits and risk assessments among the requirements that must be addressed ahead of key deadlines.
The first reporting period covers H2 26, before full calendar-year reporting begins in 2027. Annual emissions reports must be verified by 31 March 2027, while allowances covering the relevant reporting periods must be surrendered by 30 April 2028.
Normec noted that the penalty for failing to surrender sufficient allowances was £100 per allowance, in addition to the outstanding obligation to surrender them.
The scheme covers emissions generated while ships are at berth, as well as those produced during voyages, putting port activities firmly within operators’ reporting calculations.
Voyages between UK ports are covered in full, while different rules apply to international voyages, and services between Great Britain and Northern Ireland.
For international voyages arriving at UK gateways, emissions from inbound port activities must be accounted for, even where the voyage itself is excluded from the scheme, according to the presentation.
Offshore vessels are expected to join the regime in 1 January without a phase-in period, adding another segment of the maritime industry into the compliance framework.
And the scheme’s scope could widen further, with a proposal to include 50% of emissions from international voyages, although no outcome had been announced following a consultation at the time of the presentation.
A registered shipowner is the default maritime operator responsible for compliance. An international safety management (ISM) company can assume that responsibility only if specified conditions are met, including a formal delegation.
Delegations must be recorded for each ship, cannot be backdated, and changes in responsibility must be communicated through the reporting platform within 14 days. Operators must also keep fleet records current, and update monitoring plans when ships enter or leave their fleets.
The webinar noted that, unlike the EU maritime emissions monitoring, reporting, and verification system, the UK scheme requires monitoring plans to be approved by the regulator rather than the verifier, creating an additional step for operators preparing for implementation.

source_document.body:
BELGRADE, Serbia — One of Europe’s key arms purchasers, Serbia, is likely to slow down procurement and investigate the probity of recent buys after a student-led protest movement ousted the country’s long-time strongman leader in a surprise election win on Sunday.
A group formed by students to battle alleged corruption in Serbia trounced Aleksandar Vucic at the polls by half a million votes, signaling exasperation with Vucic’s 12-year, increasingly authoritarian rule.
Vucic sought to punch above his weight on the international stage by playing Russia off against the European Union by seeking EU membership and supplying arms to Ukraine, but also refusing to apply sanctions against Russia.
He also acted as a bridgehead into the Balkans for China, signing major infrastructure deals with Chinese firms.
Vucic accompanied his outreach to Europe and China with large arms purchases, including buying 12 Rafale jets from France and FK-3 and HQ-17A air defense systems as well as CH-92 and CH-95 drones from Beijing .
Serbia also purchased Hermes drones from Israel and struck a deal with Elbit to assemble drones in Serbia.
According to SIPRI, Serbia spent around 1.12 billion euros on arms procurement in 2025 and nearly 3.65 billion euros in the period 2021-25.
Russian President Vladimir Putin (R) walks with Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic for a meeting at the Diaoyutai State Guesthouse in Beijing on Sept. 2, 2025. (Maxim Shemetov/POOL/AFP via Getty Images)
In January, Vucic announced he would double Serbia’s military capabilities within 18 months.
But on Sunday, he was voted out of office after students put up their university professors as candidates in a national election, forging a political party with huge support but no named leader.
Katarina Djokic, a researcher at SIPRI, told Defense News the new government would stay busy in the short term focusing on expunging Vucic’s firm grip on business and politics at home, with defense pushed further down the to-do list.
“The new government will have other priorities — prominently, delivering on anti-corruption policies and reestablishing functioning political institutions, which will be challenging enough. Under such conditions, there could be less resources and less political consensus for major defense projects,” she said.
“What could reasonably be expected is a slowdown in armament expenditures in the couple of years to come,” she added.
Djokic noted that the Student List’s manifesto talks of continuing to develop its layered air defense and modernizing Serbia’s air force, but she pointed to a stress on improving the lot of personnel, with a pay rise promised.
The manifesto talks of remedying a “scarcity of qualified personnel.”
The document also says an inquiry will be set up to pore over the paperwork of Vucic’s arms accords looking for corrupt deals.
“A new commission is being formed – an independent, interdepartmental government commission for irregularities, abuses and corruption in the production, procurement and export of weapons, as part of a general audit of the previous regime’s contracts,” it states.
The manifesto adds, “We will modernize defense industry factories and turn them into smart factories, establish a National Center for Military Electronics in cooperation with technical faculties, and launch a defense software program.”
The new government may not be so well disposed to defense deals with Israel. In the manifesto’s section on foreign policy it states, “We will not be complicit in the systematic attempt to destroy the Palestinian people that Israel is carrying out in the Gaza Strip.”
Vucic was adept at linking his arms build-up to tensions with neighboring Kosovo , which was formerly a part of Serbia and never acknowledged as an independent state by Serbia.
“Depending on the new government’s regional relations, there may be less incentive to use regional tensions and “arms races” as a pretext for ordering more arms, and more advanced arms,” said Djokic.
The Student List’s manifesto does however suggests the new government will keep up demands that Kosovo is reintegrated into Serbia.
“We will fight for the preservation of Kosovo … as part of Serbia,” it states.

source_document.body:
PARIS — Switzerland narrowed down the choice of the country’s second future long-range air defense system to either Israel’s Barak MX system or the French-Italian SAMP/T NG, while also sticking to plans to buy the United States’ Patriot air-defense system.
The federal government asked the defense department to continue evaluating the Barak MX developed by Israel Aerospace Industries and the SAMP/T NG from the Eurosam joint venture between MBDA and Thales, it said on Wednesday . In addition to technical, military and weapon-related aspects, the choice takes into account foreign-policy and economic-policy considerations, the federal council said.
Switzerland said in May it would evaluate long-range air-defense systems from manufacturers in Germany, France, Israel and South Korea, with a preference for a system produced in Europe, after delivery of the Patriot system was delayed by several years.
“The Federal Council considers it necessary to strengthen the country’s air defense to address the deteriorating geopolitical situation,” the government said. “Long-range ground-to-air defense systems are indispensable for this purpose, with an adequate supply of ammunition.”
The long-range systems, combined with short-range and medium-range systems as well as fighter aircraft, will allow Switzerland to counter attacks from a distance, including ballistic missiles, the government said.
“It is important that Switzerland can quickly equip itself, in addition to the Patriot, with a second system that meets its needs in light of the threat, allows to expand the protected area, and reduces dependence on a single supplier or a single supply chain,” the council said.
The council said it considered bids from four manufacturers in France, Israel and South Korea.
While the U.S. is prioritizing Patriot delivery to countries that have supplied their own systems to Ukraine, abandoning the Patriot purchase without a replacement system is not an option in the current situation, according to the government. It said discussions with the U.S. on delivery of Patriot systems are continuing.
Parliament is scheduled to review a government proposal for an additional 24 billion Swiss francs (US$30 billion) in defense and security spending during its winter session, including 6 billion francs to finance the second long-range air-defense system and a portion of the additional costs for Patriot, the federal council said.
Once the evaluations are complete and parliament has decided on funding for the armed forces, which is expected in early 2027, the council will decide on additional appropriation for the Patriot system and the next steps for the second long-range air-defense system, it said.
Switzerland previously agreed to buy Diehl Defence’s IRIS-T SLM system for medium-range air defense and the Oerlikon Skynex short-range system from Rheinmetall.

source_document.body:
Kenco’s 2026 Peak Season Consumer Report found that 43% of the North American consumers it surveyed plan to spend more this peak season. That’s more than double the 20% who said so a year earlier. Another 39% expect to spend about the same, and 18% plan to spend less, down from 28% in 2025.
The bigger budgets come with bigger supply chain expectations someone has to pay for. In the survey, 73% of respondents said they consider free shipping standard when shopping online, 48% expect two-day delivery, 47% expect free returns, and 40% expect real-time tracking.
Most of the goods are already here. The Global Port Tracker that the National Retail Federation and Hackett Associates released Oct. 8 shows August was likely the busiest import month of 2026, and NRF said most holiday merchandise has arrived.
Frank Loewen, senior vice president of retail operations at the Chattanooga, Tennessee-based third-party logistics provider , said the jump in planned spending can be read two ways.
“One, I am in a better place, so I can afford to spend more,” Loewen told FreightWaves. “Another one is I’m expecting prices to go up, but I still have to buy my kids presents, so I’m just going to end up spending more than I did last year for potentially the same item.”
Some of Kenco’s higher-end customers are seeing more volume than in the last couple of years, which Loewen said could reflect a K-shaped economy. Price pressure shows up elsewhere in the survey: 45% of respondents named import tariffs as a cost concern.
This year’s survey, fielded in August 2026, polled more than 350 consumers, up from 250 for Kenco’s 2025 report .
Free shipping costs shift to 3PLs
Loewen traced the free-shipping expectation to Amazon, whose Prime memberships give it income to offset the shipping it gives away. That has put pressure on 3PLs and retailers, he said.
“Nothing is free, right?” Loewen said. “When customers are not charged directly, those costs are absorbed elsewhere in the value chain.”
Kenco’s response is to place inventory as close to population centers and carriers as possible, he said, then line up carrier rates that leave flexibility for the last mile.
Free shipping also changed how shoppers order, and that feeds returns. Only 5% of respondents said return policies don’t matter when deciding where to shop.
“Consumers may order additional items when shipping carries no additional charge, then return what they don’t keep and expect their refunds as quickly as possible,” Loewen said.
More retailers now charge for returns, he said, while steering shoppers to drop-off points at malls and supermarkets. Fees carry their own risk: 32% of respondents said they would stop shopping with a retailer after encountering hidden fees.
Shoppers tie trust to stock accuracy
In the survey, 80% of respondents said inaccurate stock levels hurt their trust in a retailer.
Retailers once filled online orders from a single warehouse, Loewen said. Now they draw on inventory in stores and several warehouses at once.
“So the idea of having accurate, location-level inventory is essential because customers can see product availability before placing an order,” he said. “They may not know which store or distribution center will fulfill it, but the item has to be available within that network.”
Loewen said Kenco’s warehouse management systems send real-time inventory data to customers’ Shopify storefronts, order management systems, or enterprise resource planning software, and its cycle counts hold accuracy at 99.9% in many cases.
Kenco leans on robotics to scale for peak
Adding peak capacity once meant bringing in large numbers of workers or installing conveyors and automation sized for a single season, Loewen said.
“Traditionally, operators had to build labor and infrastructure capacity around their highest seasonal demand,” he said. “Flexible automation now allows us to scale throughput without carrying that excess capacity throughout the year.”
Kenco now uses goods-to-person systems in which robots bring product to pickers. The company announced plans in 2024 for a 130-robot AutoStore system serving multiple e-commerce customers at its Jeffersonville, Indiana, distribution center. AI tools now group orders so products are picked more efficiently, work people once did by hand, Loewen said.
“People are still involved and responsible for operating the technology,” he said. “But with automation, we’re able to fulfill orders more efficiently than we could in the past.”
Why it matters: Shoppers plan to spend more this peak, and 73% still treat free shipping as standard. Kenco is moving inventory closer to customers and leaning on robotics to absorb those costs, while its own executive says part of the spending jump may reflect higher prices.

Gran Turismo 7 Will Let You Drive a 1954 Maserati Spyder for Free for Two Weeks
21 photos
Photo: autoevolution
I’m currently experiencing some unexpected back pain which means I can’t really get out of bed. Luckily for me, both the TV and PS5 are in my bedroom and today Gran Turismo 7 has a new Online Time Trial for us to go through. It’s nice being able to play and work without having to sit at a desk.
I didn’t get any reward from the Time Trial that concluded today, and I honestly even forgot what it was. Once I saw the photo of the Xiaomi Vision Gran Turismo I realized what had happened.
I’m frankly upset Polyphony chose this car for the first ever Time Trial at Sugo, where any Japanese car in the game would have been the perfect match. I didn’t even buy his VGT, despite the Seasonal Menu and 5-Star Roulette Ticket reward available for it.
While I’ve almost accepted the idea that electrification is here to stay in the real world, I won’t accept it being shoved down my throat in the virtual realm.
If you feel the same way, you’ll be happy to know that the car we can drive for free for the next two weeks is a classic racer from the 1950s that’s typically worth almost three million credits! But first, I needed to warm up!
McLaren F1 GTR - BMW '95 Photo: autoevolution I paid 20 million credits for the McLaren F1 GTR -BMW ‘95 last week and I intend to get my money’s worth by driving it around every single circuit in the game. It’s by no means a purely financial decision, as it’s exhilarating to drive despite being 30+ years old.
It was fast enough for a 6:44 lap of the Nurburgring Nordschleife last week, and I’m curious to see how much I can improve after 20 to 30 more attempts. Anyway, I didn’t change a single thing about it for today’s time attack session.
In hindsight, it’s not the perfect idea for the first lap of the day especially since I’m not that familiar with Blue Moon Speedway’s Infield A layout. Experiencing this combo further reassures me that GT7 is a much better game than NASCAR 26 , and I challenge anyone who thinks otherwise to at least play both before making up their mind on the topic.
I lapped Infield A in 71 seconds on my second attempt, and I’m certain someone who’s more experienced can get a lot closer to the one minute marker.
Caterham Seven Superlight R500 '08 Photo: autoevolution Going from 600 bhp to just 63 bhp might seem a bit extreme, until you realize the Caterham Seven Superlight R500 weighs less than half of what the McLaren does.
That’s also partly due to the fact that the one I used today doesn’t have the original engine anymore. And I feared it might feel painfully slow down the acceleration zones of the fictional tri-oval venue.
It obviously topped out at 93 mph/150 kph, but even at that point there’s still a much better sense of speed in GT7 than you get in NASCAR 26 at 150 mph (241 kph).
Anyway, less is sometimes more, and you’ll forget about the slow straight sections once you hit the corners! I’d say this car is an excellent choice for someone who’s still in his early days of sim racing and needs to ease into it.
Ford Mustang 2015 American Racer Photo: autoevolution While a lap in the Caterham took me one minute and 40 seconds, I knew the Ford Mustang Racer would be considerably faster with 800 bhp on tap. That’s about what you’d expect from a 2026 NASCAR racer.
I couldn’t just train at this venue without using some good old American muscle, right? I went with a Cheez-it livery for the job, and soon found myself storming down the main straight at 186 mph (300 kph).
The power delivery on this thing is formidable to say the least, but the handling is not quite on par. Well, that could just be a side-effect of having driven the McLaren first, as that’s in a different league altogether.
I messed up on three different laps, either braking too late or accelerating too early out of a corner. My fastest lap was only three seconds slower than the one in the F1 GTR, and now I’m curious to see what the outcome would be if the two would go up against each other on a regular oval layout.
Ford Mustang Mach 1 '71 Photo: autoevolution Have you seen my recent Hot Wheels unboxing ? I opened a Ford Mustang Mach 1 that first showed up in toy stores in 1998, and it was easily one of my favorites out of the 10 items I took photos of.
It reminded me that I hadn’t driven my virtual ‘71 Mach 1 in a long time so that’s what I wanted to do today.
Do yourself a favor and find a solution to replace the factory-spec four-speed gearbox before any high-speed run, though.
I’m currently at 464 bhp with my supercharged setup, and it felt slightly underpowered after the Mustang American Racer. I also had to deal with some wheelspin in third gear, but it was ultimately more user-friendly if that’s what you’re looking for.
Time Trial Photo: autoevolution When I signed in today, the Time Trial had only been available for 24 minutes. Calster was already up in P1 with a 1:20.730 fast lap, while holl01 was in P2 (0.4 seconds behind). At the time of writing, over 7,000 people have signed up for the event, and only 1% of them are faster than 1:22.000. Meanwhile, the slowest (reasonable) lap time is 1:42.629.
That player needs to improve by at least 14 seconds if he plans on scoring the Bronze Record Reward! The target for Gold is quite a bit more challenging at 1:23.151, and it won’t get any easier from here. Let’s focus on the car we’ll be driving for a moment. The 1,986cc engine in this Maserati uses a rather unusual inline-six cylinder setup, with a maximum output of 166 bhp.
If you like oldschool Ferraris, you’ve certainly heard of the man who built the engine: Gioacchino Colombo. We’re obviously talking about an FR layout here, and the car weighs just 1,631 lbs (740 kg). The gearing is pretty unusual if you’re used to modern cars, as third will go all the way up to 124 mph (200 kph).
That said, don’t be afraid to use first gear in some of the tighter corners at Blue Moon Speedway, or else you’ll find yourself too low in the rev-range. Understeer can be a problem at times as I soon discovered, but other than this Maserati is plenty of fun. I secured a Bronze Record Reward after just three laps, and I might go at it again using the Logitech RS50 and the PS VR2 combo for maximum immersion.

IZMIR, Turkey — The Ministers of Defense of Bulgaria , Romania and Turkey have condemned attacks against commercial vessels in the Black Sea and call on all parties to refrain from any further actions that could endanger commercial vessels, maritime infrastructure and freedom of navigation in the Black Sea, according to the joint statement made after a meeting in Sofia, Bulgaria, on Oct. 28.
The trilateral meeting on security in the Black Sea region was also attended by the Chiefs of Defense of Bulgaria and Turkey, Adm. Emil Eftimov and Gen. Selcuk Bayraktaroglu, and the Deputy Chief of Defense of Romania, Lt. Gen. Dragos Dimitru Iakub.
The meeting signals a coordinated approach by the three NATO littoral states to the growing risks to commercial shipping and maritime infrastructure arising from the Russia-Ukraine war.
The Financial Times reported based on data from maritime security company Ambrey and the International Maritime Organization (IMO) that since the beginning of the year, more than 570 vessels have been hit in the Black Sea, killing at least 40 seafarers. By comparison, 24 deaths have been recorded in the Strait of Hormuz area for the same period.
The joint declaration highlights the Black Sea’s importance for global trade and the supply of grain fertilizers and recalls that all parties must comply with international law, including the Montreux Convention and applicable international humanitarian law, to ensure security in the Black Sea and preserve regional stability.
Bulgaria, Romania and Turkey also agreed to enhance information and intelligence sharing, improving maritime domain awareness and strengthening early warning to support security and stability in the Black Sea.
Turkish Defense Minister Yaşar Güler stated after the meeting that Turkey will maintain its current implementation of the Montreux Convention.
“I believe that the united and resolute position we have demonstrated here today, in full coordination and solidarity with our friends and allies Bulgaria and Romania, is important in clearly reminding both warring parties that the security of commercial shipping routes in the Black Sea and the safety of littoral countries constitute inviolable red lines,” Güler said.
The Bulgarian Defense Minister Dimitar Stoyanov stated that the three Black Sea countries will continue active cooperation both in a trilateral format and within NATO, in close coordination with the member states and partners of the alliance.
As the ministerial meeting was convening in Sofia, the Bulgarian Navy reported that it has successfully conducted a rescue operation for the crew of the Liberian flag merchant ship Contship Jet after it was hit by an unmanned surface vessel. The ship was 17 miles east of Cape Kaliakra in Bulgaria and bound for the port of Constanta in Romania.
The three countries will continue consultations, with the next round scheduled to take place in Ankara and Bucharest.

Dealer Buys Volvo XC90 From First Owner, Sells it 100 Miles Later for Four Digits
18 photos
Photo: Cars&Bids
Yeah, it’s not exactly the second-generation Volvo XC90 , which has been around since 2015, being facelifted two times in 2019 and 2024, but its predecessor, the original SUV.
This iteration of the family hauler was put together in Sweden, Malaysia, and China between 2002 and 2014 (2016 XC Classic in China), and was based on the Volvo P2 platform. Thus, it shared its underpinnings with the XC70, V70, S80, and S60 from that era. A single diesel engine and several gasoline units made up the powertrain family, paired with manual or automatic transmissions, depending on the configuration.
Rivaling the era’s BMW X5 and Mercedes-Benz ML, as well as other premium mid-size crossovers, the first-generation Volvo XC90 is now worth pennies on the dollar, though some say that it is built like a tank. Such a vehicle will set you back from as low as $1,500 to over $10,000 in today’s market Stateside. Beaten up examples sell for the former sum, a good / average condition car will fetch from $3,000 to $6,500, and those considered to be in excellent condition with under 100,000 miles (160,000 km) can exceed $10,000.
This 2003 Volvo XC90 is a T6, so it packs a 2.9-liter turbocharged straight-six engine. The mill developed 268 hp (272 ps/200 kW) and 280 pound-feet (380 Nm) of torque when the crossover was new. It features a four-speed automatic transmission and all-wheel drive, takes just under 9 seconds to hit 60 mph (97 kph) from a standstill, and has a 130 mph (210 kph) top speed.
Photo: Cars&Bids Finished in Black Sapphire Metallic on top of a gray interior, this machine rides on 18-inch Atlantis wheels, and features rear parking sensors, a sunroof, leather upholstery, and a folding third-row. It was offered with a clean Carfax report, meaning that there are no mileage discrepancies and no accidents in its past, and has a clean Colorado title.
But surely it cannot be perfect, can it? Actually, it is not, because it does have some chips and scratches on the outside, as well as some hail damage. The rear wiper bolt cover is missing, the fuel filler door latch is broken, and so is the central console armrest. And there is also some wear on the seats, as we can see in the shared images.
The Carfax report reveals that this old Volvo XC90 was serviced and maintained at Rickenbaugh Cadillac in Denver, and the vendor says it has 52 service records. Speaking of the vendor, they reportedly bought it in late 2024, adding roughly 100 miles (160 km) since. And before the selling dealer acquired it, it had a single owner in the papers. And it still does, the listing reveals, which makes this vehicle a lot more appealing.
The car was accompanied by three keys, the owner’s manual, and a set of rubber floor mats, and at the time of cataloging, it had 65,600 miles (~105,500 km) under its belt. Now, we already told you that the Volvo XC90 from this generation usually fetches between $1,500 and over $10,000 in today’s used car market in the United States of America, so how much do you think the pictured example got?
Photo: Cars&Bids Unless you said $6,255, then you are wrong, because this was the selling price. The vehicle was advertised on Cars&Bids as part of an online auction. The gavel hit the table on October 28, 2026, and when it did, the buyer got a great machine, this writer thinks. After all, we already told you that some say the original Volvo XC90 is built like a tank, and I am very curious to see if we can say the same about most of today’s new rides a few years from now.
Probably not, but that’s a story for another time. Meanwhile, we have to ask you whether you would ever consider buying such an SUV that is more than two decades old, and use it on a daily base, perhaps as a family hauler. Better said, would you have tried to park this one in your driveway if you came across it in time?
For $6,255, this is definitely a lot of car for the money, as that sum would otherwise get you a new electric bicycle, if your are into that kind of stuff. Or a beaten up ride, as there are literally countless used vehicles listed for a similar sum at any given moment. And to be honest, this 2003 Volvo XC90 T6 looks like it has a lot more life left in it. Not to mention that it hasn’t aged badly at all, has it?
Now, feel free to drop a line or maybe more in the comments area below and speak your mind about this old SUV , and when you are done, you should check it out in more detail on the quoted website here .

By Alex Lennane in Miami
29 October 2026
Rising airfreight yields have failed to keep pace with soaring fuel prices, squeezing freighter economics despite a sustained period of strong demand growth, according to Rotate.
Speaking at TIACA’s Air Cargo Forum in Miami this week, CEO Ryan Keyrouse warned that the strength of the global market concealed sharp differences in the financial performance of individual tradelanes and flight directions.
Rotate’s presentation showed fuel prices up 111% year on year in the final week of September, compared with a 26% increase in global air cargo yields, using Xeneta yield data.
Fuel prices fell during the Middle East ceasefire, before rising again, while yields had broadly stabilised.
“Airlines are feeling quite a bit of pressure when it comes to fuel prices, right now,” said Mr Keyrouse.
The pressure was particularly acute for freighter operations, he added. Rotate’s modelling of Boeing 777 freighter economics showed the gap between revenue and costs narrowing as fuel became more expensive.
“Some tradelanes are indeed quite negative at this point, with what’s happening with fuel and yields,” he said.
The company’s estimates for September illustrated the directional divide: Asia-North America 777 freighter flights generated a positive contribution of $2.55 per kg, against a negative $2.12 per kg in the reverse direction.
These are modelled flight contributions, rather than reported airline profits, but underline the importance of assessing the economics of the wider network.
“We all know that you make money coming one way, lose money going the other. That margin is tightening, so it makes network planning quite difficult these days,” said Mr Keyrouse.
Yield increases also varied considerably by market. Europe-Middle East yields were up 56% year on year in the final week of September, against +30% for Asia-North America and +24% for Asia-Middle East. Europe-North America recorded a 19% increase, while Asia–Europe yields rose 17%.
The squeeze comes despite what Mr Keyrouse described as a historically healthy period for air cargo supply and demand.
Demand growth had averaged approximately 9% over the past 36 months, against capacity growth of about 5%, he said, contrasting this with much of the period before 2020, when capacity expansion had outpaced demand.
But growth has become increasingly concentrated geographically and by commodity, creating additional challenges for carriers.
China’s share of global air cargo exports had increased from 27% to 34%, according to Mr Keyrouse, while ecommerce and AI-related cargo accounted for roughly two-thirds of demand growth over the past couple of years.
He suggested the wider contribution of AI could be greater still, given the associated movements of machinery and power generation equipment. That concentration has helped deepen the imbalance between Asian exports and return flows, leaving airlines to manage the cost of weaker backhaul sectors alongside higher fuel bills.
Rotate, nevertheless, expects global demand to continue expanding. Its forecast puts average year-on-year growth at 3.1% in the fourth quarter of 2026, followed by 5.1% in the first half of 2027.
The company identified continued growth in Chinese ecommerce exports to the US, AI-related technology exports from Taiwan and South-east Asia to the US, and increasing intra-Asia trade as key drivers.
Industry sentiment also remained relatively positive: 70% of respondents to Rotate’s sentiment index expected this year’s peak season to be at least as good as 2025’s.
Over the next 12 months, Mr Keyrouse said, Rotate expected demand growth of around 3.3%, broadly matching capacity expansion of approximately 3%. Freighter deliveries and conversions would drive much of the additional supply, with retirements also factored into its estimates.
However, a balance between global supply and demand would not mean individual markets were equally well supplied.
“Yes, next year there will be a global balance between supply and demand, but that is not at a tradelane level,” he said.
“You will see airlines and companies really fighting it out to find opportunities on those different tradelanes.”

By Alexander Whiteman
29 October 2026
Boluda Shipping is to acquire Samskip, yet another sign of consolidation in the shortsea shipping scene, the deal intended to create a network spanning Northern Europe, the Iberian Peninsula, Canary Islands and West Africa.
Subject to regulatory approval, the deal is expected to complete on New Year’s Day, with the combined company’s 32 vessels offering more than 750,000 teu on 18 routes across 28 countries and 21 maritime terminals, as well as five rail terminals and more than 500 trucks.
Ignacio Boluda Ceballos, chair of Boluda, said: “We have a clear vision: to lead European shortsea shipping and make our network a competitive advantage for the businesses that place their trust in us.
“Bringing Samskip’s network and expertise together with Boluda’s maritime and logistics capabilities gives us the scale and opportunities to take that ambition further.”
Mr Ceballos added that the deal focused on expanding connectivity between Europe and West Africa. The companies believe their combined networks will provide greater connectivity and more comprehensive end-to-end logistics services, a multimodal approach, seen as offering a way for customers to reduce CO2 emissions.
Samskip CEO Ólafur Orri Ólafsson said: “Samskip and Boluda are two family-owned companies with a long track-record in transport, shared values, and a long-term vision. That common ground gives us confidence in the opportunity ahead.
“By bringing our complementary strengths together, we can expand what we offer our customers while building on the expertise, commitment and service they rely on every day,” added Mr Orri Ólafsson, who will continue as CEO.
Already running joint services in Spain, the two operators have identified opportunities to combine the network, but with Samskip based in Rotterdam and Boluda having added presence there, the Dutch gateway is set to become a strategic hub.
Until the transaction closes, both companies will continue to operate independently. Boluda said it intended to invest in the combined network to increase capacity, expand connections, and support further growth.
For Samskip, it is its second sale of the year, having begun 2026 by divesting its UK and Ireland activities to Compagnie Luxembourgeoise de Navigation (CLdN), purportedly on the basis that it intended to focus on European and Nordic operations.

Heybike V1 Pro Lands with Everything You Want from an e-Bike for Just Under $2,000
16 photos
Photo: Heybike
Life is not easy these days for people in the market for electric two-wheelers, as they have so many options to choose from that, in some cases at least, could cause headaches. If the main criteria when choosing one bike over the other has to do with as many features as possible offered in a single, cheap package, then the Heybike V1 Pro might be the thing for you.
Heybike was founded about five years ago, and, even if it's based in Texas, its roots are Chinese. The crew truly stepped into the spotlight earlier this year, when it presented the V1 model .
The company says the model was so successful (no numbers are provided to back up that claim, though) that it now requires a more capable variant. Called the V1 Pro, it takes the innate capabilities of the original model and stretches them even further.
What does that mean? Well, whereas the basic setup of the Pro remains the same as the standard version, it lands on the market with double the peak power, almost 44 percent more battery capacity (which translates to 20 percent more range), 11 percent more top speed, and 50 percent higher climbing angle – because yes, this thing was not born to be used only on asphalt and level roads.
Officially, the Heybike V1 Pro is a dirt bike , and, as such, it packs the appropriate staggered wheels: 17 inches at the front and 14 inches at the rear, both of them shod in oversized Big Foot tires. The rear wheel gets over 30 percent more power compared to the regular V1 from the 8,000 W peak-power electric motor, and 250 Nm of torque.
Enough to give the e-bike a top speed of up to 50 mph (80 kph). That can be maintained for as many as 60 miles (96 km), which is the maximum range the 1,944 Wh battery pack can allow on a single charge. Speaking of that, it takes up to six hours for the pack to get back to capacity when depleted.
What makes this thing truly a dirt bike is the suspension system, which comprises a 150 mm-travel front fork and a 40 mm rear hydraulic shock. Coming it with 285 mm of ground clearance (almost 15 percent more than on the V1), the Pro can tackle inclines of up to 45 degrees.
Heybike fitted the two-wheeler with a wheelie boost assist feature, because you never know when the rider gets the urge to show off. It kicks in to help the human in charge lift the front wheel to a fixed (and undisclosed) angle.
Hydraulic disc brakes (with regenerative braking) are on deck to handle stopping, and there is even a magnetic emergency kill switch on deck that cuts power should the rider fall off the bike. At the same time, a throttle-reset safety mechanism stops power delivery to the wheels.
Heybike offers the Pro with a dedicated app that allows riders, among other things, to select one of three modes (Eco, Linear, and Sport), while an optional Bluetooth speaker is offered as an option, with the added perks of multiple simulated motorcycle engine sounds, as the company says.
The Heybike V1 Pro is already available to pre-order in the United States, where, for now at least, it goes for $1,999 for a limited period of time. If you happen to miss this window (it's unclear how long it will be open), the price jumps to $2,199.

This 2026 Porsche Cayenne GTS Depreciated Almost $40,000 in 9 Months
16 photos
Photo: Cars&Bids
What is the biggest enemy of the Porsche Cayenne ? Well, it’s not a rivaling sporty crossover. If you said “depreciation,” then you have paid attention to the title.
Take this 2026 model year GTS, for instance, which was picked up brand new by the seller in January 2026. The man paid $169,990 for the vehicle, and put it up for sale nine months later on Cars&Bids, as part of an online auction that ended on October 28, 2026. And when the gavel hit the table, this machine failed to change hands, though it sold right after for $131,500.
That’s almost $40,000 less. Or $38,490 to be more precise, which means that this Porsche Cayenne cost its first owner over $7 per mile. At the time of cataloging, the odometer read 5,400 miles (8,700 km), and you are probably wondering why the man chose to part ways with the still-new Cayenne. The answer is the Alpina XB7, which he also owns, and says that it is superior, and suits the family needs, including the extra space, better.
Given that this model is a GTS, you already know that it features a V8 engine under the hood, don’t you? It is a familiar unit with twin turbos and a 4.0-liter displacement, which produces 493 horsepower (500 ps/368 kW) and 486 pound-feet (660 Nm) of torque. The spec sheet shows that 0-60 mph (0-97 kph) is a 4.4-second affair, and the top speed on summer tires is 171 mph (275 kph).
Photo: Cars&Bids The MSRP of a brand-new Porsche Cayenne GTS is $132,400 for the latest model year, and the Turbo E-Hybrid sits at the top of the series, boasting 729 hp (739 ps/544 kW) in total. It hits 60 mph in just 3.5 seconds, and maxes out at 183 mph (295 kph). The Cayenne S E-Hybrid is found below the GTS, priced from $111,600. It has 512 hp (519 ps/382 kW) combined, is just as fast from 0-60 mph, and has a 163 mph (262 kph) top speed.
Further down the range, you will find the Cayenne S, Cayenne E-Hybrid, and the base Cayenne, with MSRPs of $108,300, $103,100, and $89,900, respectively. The entry-level model has 348 hp (353 ps/260 kW) on tap, the E-Hybrid enjoys 463 hp (469 ps/345 kW), and the S has 468 hp (475 ps/349 kW) to play with. The 0-60 mph sprint takes 5.7, 4.6, and 4.7 seconds, respectively, and the respective top speeds are 154, 158, and 170 mph (248, 254, 274 kph).
Some of the on-board gear includes the Technology Package, the Sport Package, and the Premium Plus Package. 29 photos

MG Motor launched the all-new all-electric MGU9 EV back in September 2026 and offered all the juicy details aside from pricing – now the omission has been rectified.
Last month, MG Motor Australia announced the main features and specifications of its "highly anticipated" MGU9 EV, the international version of the Maxus Terron 9 stemming from China’s SAIC Motor Corporation. MG is a well-known British automaker, established in 1942 as Morris Garages and in time became “one of the world’s most recognized automotive brands, famous for making stylish and affordable British sports cars.”
However, the present is vastly different, and the future is all about making electric mobility more accessible across international markets, with the company now a subsidiary of the Chinese automaker SAIC since late 2007. Back to the Land Down Under, which has had an official MG presence since 2016, the company is launching quite a few new models this year, such as the all-new MG4 EV Urban , the all-electric MGS6 crossover SUV, or the limited-series MGU9 Black Edition pickup truck, among others.
Now the MGU9 EV all-electric model is launching in Australia starting on October 29, 2026, with a full 3.5-ton towing capacity, “giving owners the ability to tow a caravan, boat or trailer while retaining the versatility expected of a full-size Ute.” The MGU9, by the way, is based on the Maxus Terron 9 BEV and diesel mid-size pickup truck produced by SAIC Maxus from 2024, and you can also find it as the LDV Terron 9 and the LDV eTerron 9 in Australia.
Targeting the lifestyle EV pickup truck segment, the all-new MGU9 EV is coming with dual electric motors, offering a combined 325kW and 700 Nm of torque, or 436 hp and 516 lb-ft of torque, complete with all-wheel drive and a four-wheel Electronic Air Suspension along with a 102.2 kWh LFP battery pack. Range is up to 430 km on the WLTP cycle, which is about 267 miles on a single charge.
MG also has a 236-liter frunk on the MGU9 EV , and the bed can take a standard pallet; there’s also vehicle-to-load (V2L) capability at 6.6 kW for use of power equipment through the external CCS2 outlet, and inside the cabin there are dual 12.3-inch screens, leather front seats, wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, 15W wireless charging, and an eight-speaker JBL sound system, among other things. There was one final detail that remained unknown, though: pricing.
Now MG has cleared the mystery and revealed the all-electric MGU9 EV will officially go on sale priced at AU$78,990 plus on-road costs. That’s almost $56k at the current exchange rate, but more importantly, in Australia it is the equivalent of a brand-new Toyota Land Cruiser Prado GX, which has a drive-away price of AU$78,869 with the 2.8-liter diesel turbo with 48-volt mild hybrid technology. That’s a nice lifestyle alternative, right?

Kawasaki Adds Smartride Clutch Tech to the 2027 KLE500 for the American Market, Starts at $7,999
13 photos
Photo: Kawasaki
It was earlier in October that Japanese bike maker Kawasaki announced the arrival on the European market of the new model year version of the KLE500 dual-purpose motorcycle, packing the fancy new Smartride system. And now comes confirmation that the new model will be reaching American shores as well.
In Kawasaki speak, Smartride stands for a clever new way for riders to skip using the clutch. In essence, we're dealing with a self-engaging clutch system (Kawasaki’s first) that relies on a mechanical centrifugal clutch fitted inside a conventional assembly.
This setup allows the rider to skip using the clutch when caught in stop-and-go urban traffic. For instance, when the bike's 451cc parallel-twin engine is at idle, the ride can stay put while in gear, without the rider having to pull the clutch lever. When engine speed increases, the starting clutch engages automatically and transfers power to the transmission.
When the motorcycle is moving, though, the starting clutch remains fully engaged, and the rider still has to change gears in the usual fashion.
The arrival of the Smartride system on the American market increases the number of available 2027 Kawasaki KLE500 motorcycles on the U.S. market to three, namely the KLE500 ABS, KLE500 SE ABS, and KLE500 SE Smartride ABS, which now becomes the flagship model of the range.
They all share the same mechanical components, including the trellis frame that holds everything together and the long-travel suspension system. The engine is the same as well, and it comes with no changes or upgrades from before.
The bikes can be propped on spoke wheels (21 inches at the front) shod in tubeless Dunlop Trailmax Mixtour tires. They are tied to a 43 mm KYB cartridge-type inverted fork at the front, delivering 8.2 inches of travel, and the Uni-Trak setup at the rear, allowing for 7.7 inches of travel.
The bikes are fitted with a taller adjustable windscreen now, metal- reinforced hand guards, and a large skid plate to protect the underpinnings. LED lights have been installed all around, and the reinforced rear frame allows for the fitting of two side cases and a top case.
When it comes to keeping riders in the loop with what happens with the bike, that task is handled by a 4.3-inch color TFT display that shows everything from fuel levels to service reminders.
Kawasaki will offer the new KLE500 models starting in November with rally-inspired styling and different colors. You can have a look at what each of them has to offer, including pricing, in the lines below.

The Department of Health and Human Services will support the production of six unapproved peptide products by compounding pharmacies.
Through the “enforcement discretion” policy published Wednesday , the HHS is lifting barriers to the production of peptides including BPC-157 and TB-500, products promoted in combination online as the “Wolverine stack” for muscle building and soft tissue repair. The FDA raised concerns about the safety of the peptides in 2023, noting the risk of immunogenicity.
However, the Trump administration has taken a different approach to peptides. In July, experts on the FDA’s Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee voted in favor of compounding the six peptides covered by the enforcement discretion policy. The experts voted against a seventh peptide, emideltide, also known as delta sleep-inducing peptide (DSIP) and advertised to promote slow-wave (delta) sleep among other benefits.
The HHS framed the enforcement discretion policy as a way to discourage consumers’ use of research-use-only peptides supplied by foreign manufacturers that pose safety risks. Allowing limited compounding under appropriate safeguards will give patients a more controlled alternative, HHS said. The policy is designed to “advance patient choice and freedom while appropriately protecting patient safety.”
Under the policy, state-licensed pharmacies, federal facilities and licensed physicians can compound the peptides without risking reprisals from the HHS. The policy is an interim measure to provide access to six peptides that are not on the list of bulk substances that can be compounded.
Responses to the enforcement policy split along the same lines as comments submitted to the Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee. The Alliance for Pharmacy Compounding welcomed the HHS’ action, calling it “an important step for patients.” The American Academy of Peptide Medicine hailed the policy as “a vital step toward eliminating the unsafe gray and black markets.”
Leaders at the Partnership for Safe Medicines (PSM) and PhRMA were among those to speak out against the policy. The policy “leaves Americans in a gray area as to whether peptides are safe or not,” PSM Executive Director Shabbir Imber Safdar said in a statement. Jim Stansel, general counsel and corporate secretary at PhRMA, also set out the concerns of branded drugmakers.
“It is deeply concerning that HHS is telling the FDA they should ignore the law and allow illegal compounding of unapproved peptides,” Stansel said in a statement. “Permitting access to peptides that have not been demonstrated to be safe or effective in clinical trials jeopardizes patient safety.”

There's a New Kawasaki Adventure Tourer in Town for 2027, Enter the KLE650
37 photos
Photo: Kawasaki
Earlier this week, Japanese bike maker Kawasaki announced the arrival on the American market of the 2027 KLE500, packing the company's first self-engaging clutch system, the Smartride. For the fans with a passion for dual-purpose two-wheelers that lean toward adventure, though, the big news is the arrival of the KLE650.
Derived from the KLE500 , the new motorcycle will land in February of next year on American shores complete with a larger engine, rally capabilities, and long-distance touring in the crosshairs.
Built, just like its sibling, around a trellis frame, the new motorcycle uses a liquid-cooled 649cc parallel twin engine to get going. The hardware is slightly modified compared to how it presents itself in other applications, featuring new electronic throttle valves and tuned intake and exhaust systems.
The bike does not use the Smartride system, but it does employ an assist and slipper clutch, as well as the company's quick shifter technology. Aiding the bike along are the Kawasaki TRaction Control (KTRC) and electronic cruise control, both of which are offered as standard.
The bike makes the connection to the ground with the help of spoked wheels, sized 21 inches at the front and 17 inches at the rear. Both are shod in tubeless tires of the Dunlop Trailmax Mixtour variety.
The suspension system that allows the motorcycle to tackle both smooth and less so terrain comprises a 43 mm cartridge-type inverted fork at the front with 8.3 inches of wheel travel, and the Kawasaki Uni-Trak at the rear, which delivers 7.7 inches of wheel travel.
Visually speaking, there are a number of things setting the KLE650 apart from its sibling. The adjustable windscreen, for instance, is larger by 106 mm, and so is the aluminum skid plate. The rally-inspired bodywork is larger as well, and metal-reinforced hand guards are on deck to better protect the rider. Finally, a five-inch LCD instrument panel sits front and center (the KLE500 uses a 4.3-inch screen).
When it lands in dealerships four months or so from now, the 2027 Kawasaki KLE650 will do so in two variants, ABS and SE ABS. They come with different color choices and different equipment.
The KLE650 ABS will be offered by the Japanese in a single color, Pearl Blizzard White, and with a sticker that reads $8,799. The SE ABS, on the other hand, which is the version that packs the quickshifter, the tubeless tires, and the larger windscreen, will offer two color schemes, Pearl Storm Grey and Metallic Bluish Green. The sticker for this one reads just one dollar under the $10k threshold, $9,999.
Even though the official launch of the models doesn't come until February 2027, the bikes are already listed on Kawasaki's U.S. configurator, so you can go nuts customizing your own.
